boundedLookup.note: Chen She general 周文/周章 (209 BC) already has per_2HSZH8HMYQCVF4BC08K4; Eastern Han biography subject is distinct.

cases.ownerFinding: Concrete false existing merge. p118 is the Eastern Han minister 周章字次叔 (s0271–s0289, AD 92–107) with exact primary witnesses. hanshu:001:p031 is Chen She's general from 209 BC (s0091 陳涉之將周章). No English or Chinese field conflates them; only the shared 周章 name drove the merge. Detach hanshu:001:p031 from this canonical person; retain or repoint Eastern Han members to houhanshu:038:p118 as anchor. Chronicles and offices on p118 are independently audited and unchanged.

primaryWitnessUnits.quote: 周章字次叔，南陽隨人也。
primaryWitnessUnits.zh: 周章字次叔，南陽隨人也。
primaryWitnessUnits.enLiteral: Zhou Zhang, courtesy name Cishu, was a man of Sui in Nanyang.
primaryWitnessUnits.enIdiomatic: Zhou Zhang, styled Cishu, came from Sui in Nanyang commandery.

primaryWitnessUnits.quote: 章從太守行春到冠軍，太守猶欲謁之。
primaryWitnessUnits.zh: 章從太守行春到冠軍，太守猶欲謁之。
primaryWitnessUnits.enLiteral: Zhang followed the governor on the spring circuit to Guanjun; the governor still wished to call on Xian.
primaryWitnessUnits.enIdiomatic: Zhou Zhang accompanied the governor on a spring inspection tour to Guanjun; the governor still meant to call on Dou Xian.

boundedLookup.note: per_0408FA is the classicist Minister of Agriculture 鄭眾/鄭司農; houhanshu:117:p009 is the eunuch 中常侍鄭眾.

cases.ownerFinding: Within-record false merge of two 鄭眾. s0220 代鄭眾為大司農 (Zheng Hong succeeds the classicist Minister of Agriculture in AD 83) cannot be the eunuch 中常侍 at s0285/s0288 (AD 107). Split: new local p137 holds minister surfaces and AD 83 claims from s0220; narrow p111 to eunuch surfaces at s0285/s0288 and re-anchor membership on houhanshu:117:p009 with bounded header per_0408FA kept as unresolved cousin-name, not merged.

primaryWitnessUnits.quote: 建初八年，代鄭眾為大司農。
primaryWitnessUnits.zh: 建初八年，代鄭眾為大司農。
primaryWitnessUnits.enLiteral: In the eighth year of Jianchu, replaced Zheng Zhong as Minister of Agriculture.
primaryWitnessUnits.enIdiomatic: In Jianchu 8 he succeeded Zheng Zhong as Minister of Agriculture.

primaryWitnessUnits.quote: 是時中常侍鄭眾，蔡倫等皆秉勢豫政，章數進直言。
primaryWitnessUnits.zh: 是時中常侍鄭眾，蔡倫等皆秉勢豫政，章數進直言。
primaryWitnessUnits.enLiteral: At this time the palace attendants Zheng Zhong, Cai Lun, and others all held power and took part in government; Zhang repeatedly advanced blunt counsel.
primaryWitnessUnits.enIdiomatic: Palace attendants Zheng Zhong, Cai Lun, and others then held power in government; Zhou Zhang repeatedly offered blunt counsel.

primaryWitnessUnits.quote: 及北鄉侯立，遷太傅，與太尉東萊劉喜參錄尚書事。
primaryWitnessUnits.zh: 及北鄉侯立，遷太傅，與太尉東萊劉喜參錄尚書事。
primaryWitnessUnits.enLiteral: When the marquis of Beixiang was established, he was transferred to grand tutor, with grand commandant Liu Xi of Donglai jointly recording Masters of Writing affairs.
primaryWitnessUnits.enIdiomatic: When the Marquis of Beixiang acceded, Feng Shi became grand tutor and, with Grand Commandant Liu Xi of Donglai, shared supervision of the Masters of Writing.

primaryWitnessUnits.quote: 順帝既立，石與喜皆以阿黨閻顯、江京等策免，復為衛尉。
primaryWitnessUnits.zh: 順帝既立，石與喜皆以阿黨閻顯、江京等策免，復為衛尉。
primaryWitnessUnits.enLiteral: When Emperor Shun was already established, Shi and Xi both because of currying faction with Yan Xian, Jiang Jing and others were removed by edict; again became minister of the guards.
primaryWitnessUnits.enIdiomatic: When Emperor Shun took the throne, Feng Shi and Liu Xi were cashiered for colluding with Yan Xian and Jiang Jing; Feng Shi later returned as minister of the guards.

boundedLookup.note: Lord Mengchang 孟嘗/田文 (~300–279 BC) is per_81D1T90PJP9SF2GC5KDW; Wu Qi-era chancellor 田文 in the historian's anecdote is a separate actor.

cases.ownerFinding: False merge plus chronology contradiction. s0098 is Fan Ye's 論曰 citing Wu Qi debating 田文 as Wei chancellor; Wu Qi died 381 BC. The merge with liangshu:014:p113 (Lord Mengchang) imported active hint BC 330–279 and attestation claim-222 westernInterval end 279 BC, which contradicts the Wu Qi debate context. Detach liangshu:014:p113 from this case; keep p035 as Wu Qi-era Tian Wen with primary witness 田文 at s0098 only. Narrow activeDateHints to a one-sided bound before Wu Qi's death (BC 381) or source-unknown; attestation loses the Mengchang interval. shiji:065:p026 may remain a cross-chapter analogue, not Lord Mengchang. Requires identity detachment and scoped date-audit reconciliation (claim-222, hints-p035).

primaryWitnessUnits.quote: 論曰：吳起與田文論功，文不及者三，朱買臣難公孫弘十策，弘不得其一，終之田文相魏，公孫宰漢，誠知宰相自有體也。
primaryWitnessUnits.zh: 論曰：吳起與田文論功，文不及者三，朱買臣難公孫弘十策，弘不得其一，終之田文相魏，公孫宰漢，誠知宰相自有體也。
primaryWitnessUnits.enLiteral: The appraisal says: Wu Qi debated merit with Tian Wen; Wen did not reach him in three respects; Zhu Maichen challenged Gongsun Hong with ten strategies; Hong did not obtain one of them—in the end Tian Wen ministered Wei, Gongsun ruled Han; truly they knew the prime minister has his own substance.
primaryWitnessUnits.enIdiomatic: The historian remarks: Wu Qi disputed merit with Tian Wen and surpassed him in three ways; Zhu Maichen posed ten challenges to Gongsun Hong that Hong could not meet—yet Tian Wen became chief minister of Wei and Gongsun governed Han. Chancellorship is a different art altogether.
